resolutions.researcher_notes: Value 'construction' is supported: in Feb 2024 Pakistan's caretaker cabinet approved the first phase (80 km border-to-Gwadar section), formally moving the project into the construction phase; Iran's ~900 km section is already built. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: multiple sources (The Diplomat Jan 2025; the current-ref Reuters headline 'remains stalled') note that physical construction on the Pakistani side had NOT actually broken ground as of 2024-2025 despite the approval, so 'construction' reflects the approved/nominal phase rather than active groundwork. Replaced the DEAD_LINK Reuters ref (401 bot-wall, and Wayback also 401) with four working independent outlets (World Pipelines, The Nation PK, Outlook India, The Diplomat).

StartYear1=2024 is supported as the year Pakistan approved and committed to start construction of its section (Feb 2024, 80 km border-to-Gwadar first phase). All three sources are Feb 2024 and carry the 2024 date + start-of-construction framing. Note: Iran's section construction dates to ~2011 and full commissioning remains pending, so 2024 specifically marks the Pakistani-side (re)start rather than commissioning.

FuelSource='South Pars gas field' confirmed by two independent sources: Offshore Technology (GlobalData project profile) states the pipeline 'will carry gas from the South Pars field', and GlobalSecurity.org independently names South Pars as the source field. Consistent with all coverage: gas is processed at Asaluyeh, the South Pars onshore terminal.

Route endpoints and provinces corroborated by 2+ independent sources. Iranian start: ISSI (Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, verified via pdftotext since the verifier cannot substring-match this PDF) names Bushehr; Offshore Technology places the start at the 'Pars energy economic zone' (= Asaluyeh, the South Pars onshore terminal town, which lies in Bushehr province) — so StartLocation=Asaluyeh / StartState=Bushehr / Iran is supported. Pakistani end: ISSI, Offshore Technology, and GlobalSecurity all name Nawabshah, and ISSI + Offshore Technology name Sindh — supports EndLocation=Nawabshah / EndState=Sindh / Pakistan. Minor wording note: the exact token 'Asaluyeh' does not appear verbatim on the verified independent pages (they say 'Pars energy economic zone'/'Bushehr'), but the identification is unambiguous.

SegmentCost=$7,500,000,000 USD supported by three independent sources each carrying the '$7.5 billion' figure (Offshore Technology/GlobalData, Iran International, Outlook India). This is the widely cited total project cost; SegmentCostUnits=USD confirmed. Note the figure is the whole-project estimate (not a segment-specific cost) and long predates recent phase-cost estimates (e.g. ~$158M for the 80 km Gwadar first phase).

Owner1='Iran Ministry of Petroleum' 100% is only partially supported. ISSI (verified via pdftotext) and other coverage attribute the Iranian section to the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), which is a wholly state-owned subsidiary under Iran's Ministry of Petroleum — so ministry ownership of the Iranian portion is reasonable. TWO CONTRADICTIONS TO FLAG: (1) sources name NIGC specifically, not the 'Ministry of Petroleum' by name; (2) the '100%' ignores that the Pakistani portion (border-to-Nawabshah) is owned/built by Pakistan's Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) - so a cross-border Owner attribution of 100% to a single Iranian entity is questionable and likely should be split Iran(NIGC/Ministry) + Pakistan(ISGS). Marked medium/single-source; recommend Update review of the owner split rather than treating this as green.
